direction: Mom-test discovery: learn how this user actually handles meeting notes today. Dig into the last real instance, not hypotheticals; do not pitch.

attendee.name: Marcus
attendee.bio: Design lead, runs ~15 calls a week.

speaker: me
text: Before we get into anything, can you walk me through your last few client calls this week?

speaker: them
text: Yeah — I had three yesterday. Back to back, which is honestly pretty normal.

speaker: them
text: On the second one I completely forgot to follow up on a thing they asked about pricing.

speaker: them
text: They emailed the next day asking, and I had to scramble because my notes were a mess.

speaker: me
text: How do you take notes during a call right now?

speaker: them
text: I type into a Google Doc, but if I'm talking I miss half of it. Sometimes I just don't.

speaker: them
text: Last month I lost a follow-up entirely and the client noticed. That stung.

speaker: me
text: What did you do after that?

speaker: them
text: I tried a recording tool for a week but stopped — too much cleanup afterward.

speaker: me
text: What made the cleanup not worth it?

speaker: them
text: It gave me a wall of transcript. I just want the three things I promised to do.
